image_description: A white minibus with green, yellow, and red stripes parked on a street. Several people are standing near the front of the bus. The bus has 'MER540' written on the side and a destination sign reading 'SMACK DAVAO'. It features a boxy shape typical of Asian utility minibuses (likely a Mitsubishi L300 FB body style).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Boxy body shape noticeably shorter than a full-size bus, yet tall enough for passengers to stand or sit upright comfortably.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle exhibits the characteristic high-roof, short-wheelbase proportions of a minibus. It is clearly distinct from a full-size transit bus.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large split windshield is visible at the front, and a continuous row of rectangular passenger windows runs along the side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The roofline is significantly higher than the adjacent pedestrians. A sliding door track and handle are visible behind the front wheel arch, indicating a front/mid-body entrance.
The vertical seam and recessed handle behind the front wheel confirm the presence of a sliding side door, standard for this vehicle class.
The short hood (bonnet) ahead of the windshield indicates a front-engine layout, consistent with the van-based chassis of this minibus type.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rear flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the vehicle is occluded by the viewing angle and background elements; it cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White, yellow, or company livery paint with route markings.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bus is white with distinctive colored stripes (green/yellow/red) and text markings ('MER540', 'DAVANG'), fitting the description of company/route livery.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible wheels are proportionate to a light commercial van/minibus, featuring standard steel rims with hubcaps.
The window count (approx. 6-7 side windows) suggests a seating capacity well within the 4-10+ range typical for this class.

selected_experts.reason: To verify the specific model taxonomy (e.g., distinguishing Mitsubishi L300 FB from other vans) and confirm class alignment.
To audit the legibility and structural correctness of the text 'SMACK DAVAO', 'MER540', and the license plate, which are common failure points in AI generation.
To ensure the wheels are properly grounded and not floating or melting into the asphalt, a common artifact in vehicle generation.
To check for clean boundaries on complex protrusions like side mirrors and the sliding door track, ensuring no fusion with the background.

focus_areas: Text legibility and coherence on the destination board and side panels.
Geometric consistency of the wheel arches and tire contact patches.
Structural integrity of the side-view mirrors and windshield wipers.
Perspective alignment of the parallel lines on the bus body.
